issues.title: Deliminate selective ANTI delim joins (NOT EXISTS) with simple RHS
issues.hypothesis: q22 (152ms) runs NOT EXISTS (SELECT * FROM orders WHERE o_custkey=c_custkey) as a RIGHT_DELIM_JOIN (RIGHT_ANTI). Its RHS still contains INNER HASH_JOIN o_custkey = c_custkey(DELIM_SCAN). The Deliminator keeps that join because the LHS (customer) has a selection, and SelectionIsReplaceableByJoinFilter (src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp:81) only accepts delim_join.join_type == SEMI. Warm JSON profile of q22.m0, total CPU about 0.8s: two customer scans 0.155s + 0.160s, orders scan 0.081s (it already has a BF and emits 1.9M rows), INNER HJ with the delim keys 0.137s (1.9M -> 1.9M rows, it filters nothing), RIGHT_ANTI HJ 0.144s, delim join overhead 0.040s, plus a DISTINCT HASH_GROUP_BY 0.012s. E0021 showed the same mechanism for SEMI: a plain join plus runtime join filters (min/max + BF on the probe scan, enabled for RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI in E0021) gives the same reduction without the extra join. With ANTI accepted, orders goes from scan+BF straight into a RIGHT_ANTI built on the 190k filtered customers. That removes the 0.137s inner HJ, the delim materialization/dedup and the delim scan.
issues.plan: In src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp, SelectionIsReplaceableByJoinFilter: accept delim_join.join_type == JoinType::ANTI as well as SEMI. Keep every other guard unchanged (one delim get, one join, INNER/SEMI child join with only colref = colref conditions, SubqueryIsSimple RHS). Optimize() then removes the join with the DelimGet. RemoveJoinWithDelimGet adds IS NOT NULL on the replacing columns. ConvertNotDistinctToEqual turns NDF into = when the RHS column is non-null, so the join filters can be generated (NDF conditions are skipped in JoinFilterPushdownOptimizer::GenerateJoinFilters). Before relying on the NDF->= conversion for ANTI, check semantics: an LHS row with a NULL key must still be emitted, both in ANTI (probe side LHS) and in RIGHT_ANTI (build side LHS, emitted by the unmatched-build scan). Check how JoinHashTable handles NULL build keys for RIGHT_ANTI (null_values_are_equal / the build-side null filtering in join_hashtable.cpp). If NULL build keys are dropped for RIGHT_ANTI, do not convert to = for ANTI; it may then need an explicit IS NOT NULL OR ... rewrite, or just skip the conversion and accept no BF. Tests: (1) a temp table customer-like with NULL keys plus NOT EXISTS over a table with NULL fk values; compare against SET disabled_optimizers='deliminator'. (2) q22 results unchanged. (3) A NOT EXISTS with an extra non-equality correlated predicate (q21 shape) must keep the old plan. Use the JSON profile trick to confirm the INNER HJ and DELIM_JOIN are gone from q22 and that the orders scan still has the BF.
issues.expected_gain: q22 -12..-20% (about 0.18s of 0.8s CPU removed). Geomean about -1%. Possibly hidden NOT EXISTS templates (q21-like ones stay unchanged because of the equality-only guard).
issues.generality: Any correlated NOT EXISTS with a simple equality correlation and a filtered outer query (anti-joins against fact tables are very common). Could be slower when the outer selection is very selective and the BF auto-disables. In that case the old delim join reduced the RHS before an expensive RHS subtree. SubqueryIsSimple limits the RHS to scans/filters/projections/inner joins, so the extra cost is bounded.
issues.risk: Medium-low. One-line gate change on a path already proven for SEMI in E0021. Main risk is NULL-key semantics for ANTI after the NDF->= conversion; the plan includes explicit tests.

## Memory (gen2)

## State
- gen1 (r1-r16): accepted E0001 JoinDependent rule order (q19), E0002 contains() selectivity (q09), E0003 perfect HJ RIGHT (q13), E0005 BF first key multi-key HJ (q09), E0006 key-set range filter through compress projs (q18), E0007 exact bitmap BF, E0011 semi-join estimate, E0012 OR-of-ranges mask, E0014 FSST simple decode + substring prefilter (q13), E0016 DELIM_GET-build BF (q22 -20%). Best 1.281x.
- gen2 r1+r2: E0017/E0018 (no CM on hash-join keys) RETIRED twice: hidden validation regressed. DEAD.
- gen2 r3/r4: E0019 (deliminate SEMI) and E0020 (exact BF through CM offset) each retired alone.
- gen2 r5: E0021 = bundle E0019+E0020 ACCEPTED (q04 -26..-35%, q09 -12%). Watch q07 (offset BF on orders orderkey on top of custkey BF).
- gen2 r6: E0022 ACCEPTED: exact-BF small-range floor (1<<22) gave geomean -9.9%, q17 -37%, q19 -35%, q08 -19.5%, q02 -19%. Best 1.476x.
- gen2 r7: DISPATCHED "Deliminate selective ANTI delim joins" (allow ANTI in SelectionIsReplaceableByJoinFilter) for q22. If it is retired for noise alone, bundle it with another small win.
- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from a PREVIOUS evolve run on this codebase. Treat them as strong measured priors, not landed code.
- .dbe/issues.md: the first 3 issues are stale (already landed). The "aggregate CM skip q13" issue is DEAD. The RIGHT_SEMI join filters issue landed in E0021.

## Acceptance lessons
- Acceptance needs BOTH: some template faster beyond its noise AND a visible geomean that improves. Bundle verified wins.

## Measured this round (r7)
- q13 eager aggregation (pre-aggregate orders by o_custkey before the LEFT join, re-aggregate above it), tested as a manual SQL rewrite: 522-536ms vs 552-560ms, only about -4%. NOT worth an optimizer rule. DEAD.
- q22 warm CPU (~0.8s): customer scans 0.155+0.160 (substring IN filter), orders scan 0.08 with BF, INNER HJ with delim keys 0.137 (filters nothing), RIGHT_ANTI 0.144, delim overhead 0.04.
- HJ build cost: a 7.2M-row build of orders (date filter) with a tiny probe takes 0.91s CPU warm, about 126ns/row, and dominates that query. It is the next big generic target (q03, q05 and q09 all have orderkey HJs with large builds). Prior "HJ prefetch no gain" applies; an idea would be radix-partition-local pointer-table inserts. Unverified.
- dbe-tool profile <instance> output looks COLD (q03 reported 0.594s total vs 202ms bench). Prefer the warm JSON trick for operator timings.
- No PK/UNIQUE constraints in the TPC-H schema (duckdb_constraints is empty), so uniqueness-based rewrites are impossible.
- q05: the l_orderkey BF has 455k keys over a 60M range, just above the 128 bits/key exact cap, so it stays hashed. Hashed BF lets 2.03M rows through vs 1.82M true matches. Raising the cap would give only about 10% fewer rows. Low value.

## q17 analysis (r6)
- Solved by E0022.

## How to get full operator timings
- dbe-tool sql "<warm query>; <warm query>; SET enable_profiling='json'; SET profiling_output='/home/shresth/dev/db_evolve/work/slots/slot0/.dbe/scratch_x.json'; <query>" then Grep '"operator_timing"|"operator_name"|"operator_cardinality"' in that file. /tmp is NOT readable.

## Key finding: CM on join keys blocks the BF
- physical_hash_join.cpp FinalizeFilters: BF only if !has_cast && no storage_offset, except an exact BF through the offset on cond 0 (E0021). A hashed BF is never pushed through an offset.
- Exact BF: TrySetExactBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:897), caps EXACT_BF_MAX_BITS_PER_KEY=128, EXACT_BF_SMALL_RANGE=1<<22, MAX_RANGE=1<<32. InsertExact/LookupExact in bloom_filter.hpp (atomic fetch_or). Hashed BF: 12 bits/key, pow2 size.
- PushRangeSetFilter (gap-split ranges) only for 50 < keys <= 3200.

## Measurement lessons
- The first 2-3 runs of a query in a process are slow (warm-up, about 2x). Alternate A/B/A/B.
- Do NOT wrap in count(*): it changes the plan. Use a temp view + `from v`.
- dbe-tool bash: no pipes, no shell variables, no $(...).
- Bench noise is ±10-20% per template on identical code (q19, q08, q03, q14 worst).
- In long bench sequences q18 is ~10% slower after q09/q13 (a bench-process artifact, E0013).

## Profile snapshot (r7): q13 551, q18 546, q09 462, q05 274, q03 202, q08 187, q07 186, q16 185, q04 178, q14 170, q22 152, q17 149, q19 113, q02 62. Geomean 205.2.
- q13: inner agg on c_custkey 3.08s CPU (15M -> 1.5M groups), orders scan 2.65s (NOT LIKE), decompress/compress pair 0.80s (folding it was a measured no-gain before), RIGHT HJ 0.58s.
- q03: lineitem scan 2.24s CPU (60M rows, shipdate filter + exact BF -> 301k rows), HJ on l_orderkey 0.75s (cold numbers).
- q18: 15M-group agg dominates (exhausted).

## Dead / exhausted
- CM join-key removal (E0017/E0018), HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ, bitpacking select, BF on sparse perfect HJ, hashed BF through CM offset, q13 eager aggregation: ~0% or worse.
- Large perfect HA: real q13 gain (-20%), but the bench flags q18 each time (artifact). Possible retry: a shared table with striped updates, to shrink the memory footprint.
- FSST DecompressVector path is not hot (enable_fsst_vectors is off).

## Next candidates
1. (dispatched r7) ANTI deliminator for q22.
2. HJ build throughput (126ns/row on large builds): look at JoinHashTable::Build / InsertHashes in join_hashtable.cpp and the sink-side partitioning. Measure the sink vs finalize split first.
3. q07/q14/q08 not analysed warm. Use the JSON trick.
4. q07: gate the offset BF when the scan already has a selective BF (only if q07 gets flagged).

## Codebase facts
- CM: src/optimizer/compressed_materialization.cpp + compressed_materialization/compress_*.cpp. In release, CM on a join fires only if est. build >= 1M rows and join/build ratio <= 8.
- Rule order: src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp (Deliminator runs before the join order optimizer). Scan-filter cardinality: RelationStatisticsHelper::InspectTableFilter.
- Deliminator: src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp: SelectionIsReplaceableByJoinFilter (:81, SEMI only), ConvertNotDistinctToEqual (:106), SubqueryIsSimple (:52).
- Join filter generation: JoinFilterPushdownOptimizer::GenerateJoinFilters (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp). NDF conds are skipped. DELIM_GET build => build_side_has_filter.
- HT pointer table sized PointerTableCapacity(Count()) (join_hashtable.cpp:787). BF inserts at join_hashtable.cpp:774/841-852.
- Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp. Perfect HA: plan_aggregate.cpp. FSST: src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp.
- Noise thresholds: q16 ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%, q14 ~5.1%; q04 ~20%; q08/q17 ±5-15%.
- Budget is tight (~$4/session): read memory, the ledger tail and the profile head, then dispatch.
